source_title: Malaysian customs seize $12.1 million in advanced AI chips inside 30 server units at Kuala Lumpur airport - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Malaysian customs authorities have seized advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth about $12.1 million concealed inside 30 server units at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, as investigators close in on a suspected syndicate believed to be smuggling high-performance semiconductors through the country, as reported by Reuters. The seizure comes amid heightened scrutiny of the movement of advanced AI chips, particularly those originating from the United States, after Malaysia introduced export controls last year following pressure from Washington to curb the flow of sensitive technology into China.Falsely declared as electronic componentsAspalila said the servers were falsely declared as electronic components and shipped through Malaysia so that no restrictions would apply when they were exported to the next destination. Initial investigations found that the shipment came from an Asian country and was due to be re-exported to another country in the region, a move that required a trade permit. That permit is required under Malaysiaâs Strategic Trade Act 2010. Aspalila declined to say where the servers came from, where the chips were made or where they were headed.A suspected syndicate and a local firmAs per the Reuters report, at least five cases have been linked to the syndicate, involving seizures of chips worth more than 100 million ringgit in total, she said, adding that she could not give more details because the investigation is continuing. TRT World, citing officials, described the latest bust as the fifth case this year involving a syndicate smuggling advanced AI chips, with the total value above $24 million. A Malaysian company that helped facilitate the shipment has been called in to assist with the investigation. In June 2026, airport officers seized 72 server units under similar false declarations, valued at about $12.93 million.Probe focuses on wider networkCustoms investigators suspect the shipment is linked to a broader smuggling network responsible for a similar attempt that authorities intercepted in June. According to officials, at least five cases have been connected to the suspected syndicate, involving seizures of semiconductors worth more than 100 million ringgit in total. Authorities declined to provide additional details because of the ongoing investigationExport controls on US-origin chipsThe seizure comes against the backdrop of Malaysiaâs export controls on advanced AI chips. Malaysia imposed controls last year on the movement of US-origin advanced AI chips, after pressure from the United States to stem their flow into China. The case shows how customs officials are looking closely at the servers that contain chips, their declared classification and their intended destinations, as well as at the chips themselves, according to StratNews Global. Malaysia has also opened several investigations, including one into how servers containing US-made Nvidia chips bound for Singapore ended up in Malaysia.The case highlights the increasing importance of export controls surrounding advanced AI hardware, which is critical for training and running sophisticated AI models.
